name: Interior

text: A wall of soundings. Depth, bearing, date, forty stations, sixty years.
Everything from the last four months is circled in red, and none of the circles are at sea.
They are all under the land.
The long table, and a chart of Caelora big enough to need it.
Pins in it by the hundred, and a length of string run
from the Caeloran Sea inland, further than the string was cut for.
Bound survey volumes, one per year, back sixty years.
The spine of this year's is uncreased.
Nobody has had time to read what they are writing.
A rack of pegs with four coats on it and eleven empty pegs.
A card pinned over the empty ones, in the same hand as everything else in this office:
GONE TO THE FOUNDATION. NO ILL FEELING. THEY PAY BETTER AND WE SAID SO IN WRITING.

_plan: The Concord is the small, old, underfunded regional body that has been measuring this coast for sixty years, and this is the room where it loses. Nothing in here is sinister and nobody in here is wrong; there is simply an organisation outside with better boxes, warmer coats and a wage that arrives on Friday. That contrast is the whole point of the office surviving into Act 2.
